A student was asked to use mathematical induction to prove the following statement. 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ... + (1/2)^n = 1 − (1/2)^n for all positive integers n The beginning of the student’s proof is shown below. First, show that the statement is true for n = 1: If n = 1, (1/2)^1 = 1 − (1/2)^1, so 1/2 = 1/2. Next, show that if the statement is true when n is equal to a given positive integer k, then it is also true when n is equal to the next integer, k + 1: Assume that the statement is true when n = k, so 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ... + (1/2)^k = 1 − (1/2)^k. For n = k + 1, the sum is 1/2 + 1/4 + ... + (1/2)^k + (1/2)^(k+1). By the assumption, this equals 1 − (1/2)^k + (1/2)^(k+1) = (2^(k+1) − 1)/2^(k+1) = 1 − (1/2)^(k+1).
